summary: Oil stayed the main risk: Brent closed at 108.79 and WTI at 97.82 on Oct 20, both down on the day after a week of attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz and an IEA move to speed emergency stock releases. On Oct 20 the S&P 500 closed at 7,712.76 (+0.29%), the Nasdaq Composite was flat at 26,424.82 and the Dow rose 1.0%, with the VIX at 17.3 and the 10-year yield at 5.12%; September US inflation at 3.7% keeps Fed hike odds for Oct 27-28 near a third. In Asia the chip selloff continued, with Samsung down 3.0% on the day and 8.8% on the week, MediaTek and ASM International down 9% and 13% on the week to Oct 19, while TSMC reported record quarterly profit. NOAA and WMO describe a strong El Nino, with Indonesia's ETF down about 18% on the week (unverified, see flags). Several commodity, freight and Hong Kong items could not be retrieved (see gaps).

reading.summary: UNEP's annual emissions gap report says exceeding 1.5C is imminent and unavoidable, projects a temporary overshoot, and finds national pledges far short of needed cuts.

reading.title: Q&A: Why a pivotal IPCC meeting in Ethiopia ended in 'profound disappointment'
reading.summary: Governments failed for the sixth time to agree a timeline for the IPCC's next major reports in Addis Ababa and could not agree its budget.

reading.title: ASEAN nations assessing nuclear energy option
reading.summary: Southeast Asian countries are taking a pragmatic look at nuclear power to meet rising electricity demand, delegates said at a supply chain conference in Manila.

reading.title: IAEA says Barakah drone-strike response was effective
reading.summary: An IAEA mission to the UAE found response actions were effective after Barakah unit 3 lost off-site power following a May drone strike near a generator.

reading.title: Philippines advances plans for nuclear power as energy demand rises
reading.summary: The Philippines is laying policy, regulatory and commercial groundwork for its first nuclear project, targeting 1.2 GW by 2032 and 4.8 GW by 2050.

reading.title: Norfund, Impact Fund Denmark agree to invest in Ixus Bugallon project
reading.summary: Norfund and Impact Fund Denmark will jointly take a 49% stake in Vena Energy's 500MW-peak Ixus Bugallon solar project in the Philippines.

reading.title: Cox to build $2.9bn energy and water systems in El Salvador
reading.summary: El Salvador's government has agreed a $2.9bn program with utility Cox to strengthen the country's energy and water infrastructure.

reading.title: Nightpeak Energy completes Bocanova battery storage project in Texas, US
reading.summary: Nightpeak finished the 150MW Bocanova 2 battery project in south-east Texas, bringing the site to 300MW; it began commercial service on 17 September.

reading.title: CCSA Unveils Winners Of Inaugural International CCUS Awards 2026
reading.summary: The Carbon Capture & Storage Association announced the winners of its first International CCUS Awards.

reading.title: CSIRO Scientists Are Carving A Path For CO2 Mineralization In Australia
reading.summary: CSIRO researchers are gathering evidence that could support developing CO2 mineralization in Australia.

reading.title: INPEX Secures Landmark Offshore Carbon Storage Approval In Australia
reading.summary: The Australian government declared the West Peron formation in the Bonaparte Basin a carbon storage site, with INPEX securing approval.

reading.title: UN sets steep emission cuts to reverse 1.5C overshoot by end of century
reading.summary: A UN Emissions Gap Report says cuts of close to 6% a year are needed to bring warming back under the Paris limit.

reading.title: Turkish giant sponsoring COP31 cut climate goals then cashed in on oil boom
reading.summary: COP31 sponsor Koç Holding has slipped on climate targets while its oil refiner runs at full capacity.

reading.title: Under US pressure, World Bank says it will back gas "where appropriate"
reading.summary: The US wants the World Bank to expand gas financing while campaigners want it ended; the bank's head signaled only limited support.

reading.title: Six beluga deaths cast a shadow over rescue from Canada's Marineland
reading.summary: Thirty belugas were moved from the closed Marineland park to other facilities over two months, and six have died.

reading.title: Delegates at biodiversity COP17 should follow the lead of Global South women (commentary)
reading.summary: Commentary arguing that delegates at the COP17 biodiversity summit should take their cues from women in the Global South.

reading.title: Search for the 'Asian unicorn' faces an uncertain future amid funding losses
reading.summary: The search for the saola, known as the Asian unicorn, faces uncertainty because of lost funding.

reading.title: GM to close Detroit battery-assembly plant, but not for reasons you might think
reading.summary: GM is closing a Detroit battery-assembly plant; the headline says the reason is not the obvious one.

reading.title: Plants can speak using electricity, so this startup built an AI model to decipher their language
reading.summary: A startup built an AI model to interpret the electrical signals plants produce.

reading.title: Porsche's electric Macan Turbo is an automotive existential crisis
reading.summary: A review-style piece on Porsche's electric Macan Turbo and the questions it raises for the automaker.

climate.headline: Panama Canal cuts Neopanamax draft to 47.5 feet
climate.detail: The canal authority lowered maximum Neopanamax draft to 48 ft on Aug 26 and 47.5 ft on Sep 3 on Gatun Lake projections, keeping transit numbers unchanged; later changes were not found.

climate.headline: Japan's weather agency says El Nino at record strength
climate.detail: JMA put September sea-surface temperature in its monitored Pacific patch 4C above normal, the highest since 1949 and above the Dec 1997 record of 3.7C.
climate.source: Japan Meteorological Agency, reported by Bloomberg, 2026-10-09

climate.headline: Rhine at Kaub falls to 0 cm
climate.detail: The Kaub gauge hit a record 2 cm on Sep 25 and 0 cm on Sep 30; barges sailed with sharply reduced loads. No October reading was found.
climate.source: German federal waterways authority WSA Rhein, 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-30

climate.headline: Southern Africa outlook: below-normal 2026/27 rains
climate.detail: The regional forum expects erratic, mostly below-normal rain from October to March, warmer temperatures, and risk to maize planting and hydropower inflows in Zambia, Zimbabwe and Mozambique.
climate.source: Southern African Regional Climate Outlook Forum (SARCOF-33), 25-28 Aug 2026, via SARDC 2026-09-02

climate.headline: ABARES sees 61 Mt winter crop despite El Nino
climate.detail: ABARES forecast wheat 29.9 Mt (3% above average) and barley 16.4 Mt; the Bureau of Meteorology outlook points drier for south-east Australia and south-west WA.
climate.source: ABARES September 2026 crop report, via UWA/The Conversation 2026-09-18

climate.headline: Thai floods ease; Indonesian fires keep haze over region
climate.detail: Thailand's DDPM reported 1.83 million people affected in 22 provinces and three Bangkok districts on Oct 19, with levels falling. Haze from Sumatra and Borneo fires closed schools in parts of Malaysia.
